# QueryRouter++

Multi-criteria LLM routing framework that selects the optimal model for each query using a formalized compatibility function C(q, m, w) scored across four axes: performance, cost, latency, and ecological impact.

## Stack

- Python 3.11+
- FastAPI for API server
- Poetry for dependency management
- Pydantic for data validation

## Key Directories

- `queryrouter/` — Core routing logic and API implementation
- `core/` — Compatibility scoring engine and router strategies
- `api/` — FastAPI endpoints and schemas
- `data/` — Data loaders and normalizers for the model matrices
- `data_models/` — Model benchmark matrices (performance, cost, ecology CSVs + query taxonomy)
- `config/` — Preference schemas and presets
- `docs/` — Full documentation (quickstart, scoring reference, LibreChat integration)
- `tests/` — Test suite (pytest, ≥80% coverage required)
- `notebooks/` — Evaluation and exploration notebooks
- `scripts/` — Utility scripts (OpenAPI export, data validation)

## Running Locally

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install poetry
poetry install

# Start API server (port 8000)
poetry run uvicorn queryrouter.api.main:app --reload

# Run tests
poetry run pytest

# Linting & formatting
poetry run ruff check .
poetry run black --check .
```

Interactive API docs available at http://localhost:8000/docs after starting the server.

## Project Stats

- 12 supported models across 7 providers: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT-4.1, o3), Google (Gemini), Mistral AI, Meta (LLaMA), Alibaba (Qwen), DeepSeek — source: `data_models/models_benchmark_matrix.csv`

Evaluation figures below come from an offline simulation, not production traffic: 200 synthetic queries × 12 models × 5 preference presets (seed=42), scored from the benchmark data in `data_models/` with no API calls. Method and full tables: README "Evaluation" section (https://github.com/Caezarr/queryrouter-plus-plus/blob/main/README.md#evaluation), evaluator in `training/evaluator.py`, analysis in `notebooks/exploration.ipynb`.

- Direct routing matches the oracle on 100% of the 200 simulated queries. This holds by construction: the oracle is the same all-model scorer that direct mode uses, so it measures implementation correctness, not real-world answer quality.
- 91.8% estimated cost savings vs always routing to the strongest model (balanced preset, same simulation).
- 87.5% estimated CO₂ reduction vs always-best in ecology mode (2.6M g vs 20.9M g over the 200 queries), with a −0.6% drop in the benchmark-derived performance score.
